claims.text: Schwab earns on client assets primarily through net interest revenue on uninvested client cash balances plus asset management and administration fees and trading revenue (SCHW-10K-2025#27), whereas advisor-led models earn on client assets chiefly through asset-based advisory fees charged on the value of client assets plus net interest income on client loans and deposits (MS-10K-2025#147, EDJ-10K-2025#126, RJF-10K-2025#216, BAC-TR-2025Q2#35).

Schwab's largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees, supported by the combination of its broker-dealer, bank, and asset management operating subsidiaries (SCHW-10K-2025#27). Net interest revenue is the difference between interest generated on interest-earning assets and interest paid on funding sources, and Schwab's primary funding source for those assets is uninvested client cash balances held on its balance sheet (SCHW-10K-2025#27).

Within the Wealth Management segment, Morgan Stanley's asset management revenues relate to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, generally based on the net asset value of the account (MS-10K-2025#147). Morgan Stanley defines fee-based client assets as client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets (MS-10K-2025#167).

Edward Jones's asset-based fees include advisory program fees based on the average daily market value of client assets in the program plus contractual rates, and the primary source of its asset-based fee revenue is program fees for investment advisory services (EDJ-10K-2025#126, EDJ-10K-2025#207). Edward Jones also earns revenue on clients' assets through service fees and revenue sharing with mutual fund and insurance companies (EDJ-10K-2025#23).

Merrill's GWIM business is primarily a fee-based, advice-driven model, with about 30% of its revenue coming from net interest income derived from GWIM clients' loan and deposit balances (BAC-TR-2025Q2#35). Fees earned on assets under management are calculated as a percentage of clients' AUM balances (BAC-10K-2025#249).

Raymond James's Private Client Group earns revenue by charging either asset-based fees (recorded as asset management and related administrative fees) or sales commissions (recorded as brokerage revenues) for financial planning, investment advisory, and securities transaction services (RJF-10K-2025#216). The segment also earns servicing fees from mutual fund and annuity companies and from banks to which it sweeps client cash deposits, plus net interest (RJF-10K-2025#696).

Schwab's full-year 2025 net interest revenue was $11.8 billion, up 28% from 2024 (SCHW-10K-2025#130), and its client transactional sweep cash balances ended September 2026 at $492.8 billion (SCHW-PR-2026-10-15-01#7).
Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management segment reported net interest income of $2,228 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (MS-SUPP-2026Q3#13).
Edward Jones reports net interest and dividends revenue of $865 million in 2025, a decrease of $86 from 2024 (EDJ-10K-2025#140).
For full-year 2025, GWIM reported net interest income of $7,197 million, up from $6,969 million in 2024, with a net interest yield of 2.32% for 2025 (BAC-10K-2025#244).
Raymond James reported combined net interest income and RJBDP fees from third-party banks of $658 million for the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026 (RJF-TR-2026Q2#16).

Schwab's asset management and administration fees totaled $6.5 billion in full-year 2025, up 14% from 2024 (SCHW-10K-2025#130). These fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions (SCHW-10K-2025#27).

Morgan Stanley reports an average fee rate on total fee-based client assets of 63 basis points for 2025 (MS-10K-2025#177), and Wealth Management asset management revenues of $18,627 million for full-year 2025 (MS-10K-2025#169).
Edward Jones's total asset-based fee revenue was $12,408 million in fiscal 2024, and its advisory programs fees were $9,463 million in fiscal 2024 (EDJ-10K-2025#237).

Merrill (BAC) reported GWIM asset management fees of $15.4 billion for 2025, up 12 percent (BAC-10K-2025#246); for shares in a fee-based program it charges fees comparable to RIA pricing, typically 1.00% to 1.40% on assets managed and as high as 1.75% (MER-TRADE-2026-09-29-RB-01#7).

Raymond James's fee-based/advisory revenue is recorded as asset management and related administrative fees, earned for asset management and related services generally based on the values of PCG client assets in fee-based accounts (RJF-10K-2025#411); Private Client Group asset management and related administrative fees were $5,980 million for the twelve months ended September 30, 2025 (RJF-SUPP-2025Q3#12).

Schwab's trading revenue is comprised of commissions, order flow revenue, and principal transactions revenue (SCHW-10K-2025#309); it reported total trading revenue of $1,215 million in the second quarter of 2026 (SCHW-10Q-2026Q2#59).

Morgan Stanley reported Wealth Management transactional revenues of $4,588 million for fiscal year 2025 (MS-PR-2026-01-15-01#10), where commissions and fees arise from client transactions including equity securities, insurance products, mutual funds, alternative investments, futures and options, plus order flow payments (MS-10K-2025#146).
